blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI — the retrieval, permissions and economics work that decides whether assistants get trusted.

Foundation models are converging. What separates a trusted assistant from an abandoned demo is everything around the model: retrieval that cites its sources, permissions inherited from your estate, freshness you can enforce, and a unit economics line your CFO believes.
These theses are argued from programs in flight — assistant rollouts, eval harnesses, cost-per-task baselines — not from a content calendar.

items: The retrieval layer is the moat, not the model
Foundation models are converging on capability; the durable advantage sits in retrieval, permissions and freshness.
GenAI unit economics: the metric nobody tracks
Cost per resolved task, not per token, is the real unit of GenAI economics.

blocks.x: Bring the assistant your teams stopped using — we will show what the retrieval layer was missing.
